headline: 52 sent to jail over alleged August 15 sabotage plot in Bashundhara
summary: A court has ordered 52 people to be imprisoned following a police raid in the Bashundhara residential area, where they were allegedly planning sabotage for August 15.
details: A Dhaka court has sent 52 individuals to jail on charges of planning sabotage in the capital's Bashundhara residential area. Two minors, Ishan and Hasib, were sent to the Tongi Child Development Center.
The order was issued by Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Ariful Islam on Friday, as confirmed by SI Kamal Hossain of the DMP's prosecution division.

Police conducted a raid on Thursday night at a residence in Block M, Road 28 of Bashundhara. Authorities claim the suspects are linked to the banned Awami League, Jubo Mohila League, and Chhatra League.

According to police, the suspects had gathered in a flat on the second floor to plan sabotage for August 15. During the raid, police seized three banners mentioning a discussion meeting and Milad Mahfil for the date.

The case filed by Vatara Police Station SI Asaduzzaman under the Anti-Terrorism Act alleges that the suspects were shouting anti-government slogans and planning to create instability and panic in the country.
The investigation officer, SI Mohammad Hafizur Rahman, requested the suspects be kept in jail to prevent them from going into hiding and to facilitate further interrogation.

headline_marked: 153-run lead: [[Bangladesh take control]] of Darwin Test against Australia
headline: 153-run lead: Bangladesh take control of Darwin Test against Australia
summary: Tanzid Hasan's historic first Test century and a dominant Day 2 performance leave Australia under immense pressure.
details: Bangladesh ended Day 2 of the Darwin Test with a commanding 153-run lead, finishing at 351 for 6. This marks their second-best total in 13 Test innings against Australia.
The highlight of the day was Tanzid Hasan's maiden Test century. The 25-year-old opener played patiently for over five hours, scoring a century before being caught by Mitchell Starc.
Bangladesh's dominance was built on key partnerships, including a 102-run stand between Tanzid and Mominul Haque, and a 93-run partnership with captain Najmul Hossain Shanto.

Australia's bowling attack struggled to contain the visitors, though Steven Smith claimed three catches at second slip, equalling Joe Root's record for the most catches by a non-wicketkeeper in Test cricket.
At stumps, Mehidy Hasan Miraz (32*) and Hasan Mahmud (13*) remained unbeaten, adding 43 runs for the seventh wicket on a pitch that is becoming easier for batting.
Former Australia captain Ricky Ponting described the Australian dressing room as a 'nervous' place, stating that the pressure is now firmly on the batters to avoid a major upset.
caption:
A 153-run lead and a historic century! Bangladesh is dominating the Darwin Test, leaving Australia 'nervous'.

Bangladesh ended Day 2 of the Darwin Test with a commanding 153-run lead, finishing at 351 for 6. This marks their second-best total in 13 Test innings against Australia.

The highlight of the day was Tanzid Hasan's maiden Test century. The 25-year-old opener played patiently for over five hours, scoring a century before being caught by Mitchell Starc.

Bangladesh's dominance was built on key partnerships, including a 102-run stand between Tanzid and Mominul Haque, and a 93-run partnership with captain Najmul Hossain Shanto.

Australia's bowling attack struggled to contain the visitors, though Steven Smith claimed three catches at second slip, equalling Joe Root's record for the most catches by a non-wicketkeeper in Test cricket.

At stumps, Mehidy Hasan Miraz (32*) and Hasan Mahmud (13*) remained unbeaten, adding 43 runs for the seventh wicket on a pitch that is becoming easier for batting.

Former Australia captain Ricky Ponting described the Australian dressing room as a 'nervous' place, stating that the pressure is now firmly on the batters to avoid a major upset.
